5.text: Another method of divination, nearly as much in use as the one just

6.text: spoken of, is that with a shoulder-blade, the centre of which is kept

7.text: over a small fire till it is partly carbonized, and cracks in all directions. The

8.text: details of the cracks determine the meaning of the answer. This method,

9.text: however, cannot be applied to every circumstance of life, because the indications

10.text: of the cracks are necessarily limited. Among the Reindeer Chukchee its chief

11.text: use is for determining the direction of the next moving of the camp. It is

12.text: also employed to foretell the success of a hunt or of a journey, the approach

15.text: The Reindeer Chukchee use for divination only the shoulder-blade of the

16.text: domesticated reindeer. The animal, in most cases, is killed for this particular

17.text: purpose, though the bones of every reindeer brought for sacrifice, or slaughtered

18.text: for meat, are also fit to be used. The bone is taken raw, and the meat

19.text: carefully cleaned from it. Then a small piece of burning coal is kept close

20.text: to its centre. It is fanned, by means of blowing or light swinging, till

21.text: the bone is carbonized, and gives the first crack. After the performance, the

22.text: burned place is immediately broken through and reduced to crumbs, but

23.text: the bone itself is added to the common kitchen-stock used for trying tallow.

24.text: During the fall, the shoulder-blade of the left side is used for divination in

25.text: personal or family affairs, while that of the right side is called “alien,” and

26.text: used for divination in the affairs of other people. During this period, divination

27.text: is employed, first, when changing camp after the first fall of snow, then again

28.text: about two months afterwards, when moving into winter-quarters.

29.text: In the winter time, divination is seldom used, but it is resumed in the

30.text: spring, when moving from the winter-pastures to the summer abode. This

31.text: moving is considered as “returning,” the tundra being the principal country

32.text: for the Chukchee people. It is called “descending road” (taˊhrɪ-têlaˊn), meaning

33.text: the descent from the wooded hills to the open tundra and to the sea.³ Even

34.text: the families who ascend the mountains in the direction of the glaciers of the

35.text: watershed call it by the same name. During this time, divination is used

36.text: for every new move; but now the bone of the right side is used for the

37.text: affairs of the family, while that of the left side is considered “alien.” However,
